questions.q: In the Fusion architecture, how does a subledger application like Payables produce a journal entry?
options: It writes directly to the General Ledger tables
It has its own independent journal-building code, unrelated to other subledgers
It raises a business event and Subledger Accounting builds the journal entry from rules
A human must manually type every journal entry
questions.explain: Subledger applications record business events; Subledger Accounting is the shared engine that turns those events into journal entries.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a source, in SLA terms?
options: The name of the Oracle Fusion data center
A specific piece of transaction data a rule can reference, such as the invoice amount or supplier name
The version number of the Fusion release
A user's login password
questions.explain: Sources are specific pieces of transaction data, like amount, supplier, or natural account, available for rules to reference.

questions.q: What is the relationship between an event class and an event type?
options: They are two names for the exact same thing
Event type is a broader category and event class is the specific occurrence within it
Event class is a category of transaction (like Invoices), and event type describes the specific thing that happened within it (like Invoice Validated)
Event classes only exist in Receivables, not in Payables
questions.explain: Event class groups a category of business transaction; event type narrows it down to the specific occurrence.

questions.q: What is the purpose of merging lines that would post to the same account?
options: To intentionally make the journal entry unbalanced
To delete transaction history
To keep the journal entry readable instead of listing many separate lines that all hit the same account
To avoid using accounting classes
questions.explain: Merging combines lines heading to the same account into one line, which keeps journal entries from becoming cluttered.

questions.q: How does a supporting reference differ from an account segment?
options: They are the same thing with two different names
An account segment applies to every transaction across the whole ledger; a supporting reference attaches extra detail to one specific journal line without becoming a permanent segment
Supporting references can only be used in Receivables
Supporting references replace the need for account rules
questions.explain: Account segments are a fixed part of the Chart of Accounts used everywhere; supporting references carry transaction-specific detail at the subledger journal line level.

questions.q: Structurally, what is a mapping set?
options: A report showing all journal entries for a period
A lookup table that translates one or more input values into a corresponding output value
A type of journal line rule that only applies to tax lines
A setting that controls ledger currency
questions.explain: A mapping set is a reusable lookup table: inputs on one side, the matching output on the other.

questions.q: How does an AAD relate to the accounting method covered in lesson 3?
options: They are unrelated concepts from different products
The accounting method points to one AAD per subledger application; the AAD is the object at that "per subledger application" layer
An accounting method contains dozens of AADs for every possible ledger in the world
AADs replace accounting methods entirely in recent Fusion releases
questions.explain: The accounting method references an AAD for each subledger application; the AAD is the complete rule bundle for that one application.

questions.q: Once a consultant is working on their own copy of an AAD, what changes are considered safe?
options: No changes are ever safe, even on a copy
Only changing the AAD's name, nothing else
Only Oracle Support is permitted to make any change, even to a copy
Adding new journal line rules, swapping in custom account rules or mapping sets, adding supporting references, or adjusting description rule wording
questions.explain: Once working on a copy, a consultant has full latitude to customize content because Oracle's original seeded version remains untouched elsewhere.

questions.q: Why does Oracle require validation of an AAD before it can be used?
options: Validation is optional and rarely performed in practice
Because configuration built by a person across many screens can contain gaps, like an incomplete account rule, that validation is designed to catch before live processing
Validation only checks spelling in descriptions
Validation replaces the need for account rules entirely
questions.explain: Validation automatically checks an AAD's structure for completeness and consistency to catch configuration gaps before they affect real transactions.

questions.q: What does the Transfer Journal Entries to GL process actually do?
options: It deletes Draft subledger journal entries
It moves eligible Final subledger journal entries into General Ledger as GL journal batches
It creates new accounting events in a subledger application
It validates an Application Accounting Definition
questions.explain: The process takes Final, not-yet-transferred subledger journal entries and moves them into General Ledger as journal batches.

questions.q: What common pattern do both Payables and Receivables share, according to this lesson, regarding Draft and Final accounting?
options: Neither subledger ever uses Draft mode
Final mode always runs automatically immediately after every transaction
Draft and Final modes are identical in both subledgers with no distinction
Draft accounting commonly runs close to real time for visibility, while Final accounting is typically run on a schedule or on demand once transactions are settled
questions.explain: Both subledgers typically favor near-real-time Draft accounting for visibility and scheduled or on-demand Final accounting once transactions are settled.

questions.q: Why does this lesson distinguish between fixing a single transaction and fixing a rule?
options: There is no meaningful distinction; both are handled identically
Because rules can never be the cause of an accounting error
Because a flawed rule likely affected every transaction that matched its conditions, not just the one a reviewer happened to notice first
Because only Final entries can ever be affected by a rule problem
questions.explain: If the root cause is a rule rather than bad data on one transaction, every other transaction affected by that same rule likely needs correction too.

questions.q: Why is a manual journal entry posted directly to a control account like AP Trade a particular concern for reconciliation?
options: It is never a concern; manual journals always match the subledger automatically
Because it bypasses the subledger's own record entirely, which reconciliation is specifically designed to catch
Because manual journals are always larger in dollar amount than subledger journals
Because manual journals can only be entered by Oracle Support
questions.explain: A manual journal posted directly to a control account creates a difference between GL and the subledger because the subledger never recorded it; reconciliation is designed to surface exactly this kind of gap.

questions.q: Why does the usefulness of these two reports depend directly on Chapter 2's rule-building choices?
options: It doesn't; report usefulness has nothing to do with rule configuration
Because well-built description rules and thoughtfully assigned accounting classes make report lines specific and meaningfully grouped, instead of generic and undifferentiated
Because reports can only be run if an AAD has never been modified
Because reports require a secondary ledger to function at all
questions.explain: Description rules and accounting classes, both configured in Chapter 2, directly determine how informative and well-organized these reports are.

questions.q: What happens if a required accounting attribute, like Entered Amount, has no valid assignment for an event class?
options: Nothing; required attributes are purely cosmetic
The transaction is automatically deleted
The General Ledger ignores the missing attribute and posts anyway
SLA cannot build a complete journal entry for that event class without a valid assignment
questions.explain: Required accounting attributes must have a valid source assignment, or SLA cannot construct a complete journal entry for events of that class.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that SLA configuration mistakes carry outsized risk compared to ordinary data-entry mistakes?
options: A flawed account rule can silently misstate every transaction of a given type across every ledger it serves, not just one record
Configuration mistakes and data-entry mistakes carry exactly the same risk
Configuration can never actually contain mistakes
Data-entry mistakes are always more costly than configuration mistakes
questions.explain: A single flawed rule has a much larger blast radius than a single data error, since it can affect every matching transaction until corrected.

questions.q: Why might a multinational company need more than one accounting representation of the same business events?
options: To intentionally make its books harder for auditors to read
Because different accounting standards, like local GAAP and IFRS, can require genuinely different treatment of the exact same underlying event
Because Oracle requires every company to maintain at least two ledgers
Because subledger transactions must always be entered twice
questions.explain: Different standards can require different depreciation methods, revenue timing, or account structures for the same events, which one representation alone cannot satisfy.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say Cash Management reconciliation quality depends on "everything upstream"?
options: Because Cash Management has nothing to do with AP or AR accounting

Because Cash Management reconciles bank activity against AP payments and AR receipts that were already accounted through SLA, so correct upstream account rules and supporting references directly determine how clean that reconciliation is
Because Cash Management never actually uses Subledger Accounting
Because reconciliation is unrelated to accuracy of account rules
questions.explain: Cash Management reconciliation depends on the accuracy of AP and AR accounting already produced by SLA, tying the whole design together.
